question: Why should nurses routinely discuss sexual health with patients?

options.A: Patients will otherwise never take their prescribed medications on time
options.B: Sexual health is a key part of overall physical and emotional well-being
options.C: Hospital accreditation boards require a sexual history for every single admission
options.D: It is the only way to diagnose infectious diseases in the community

explanation: Because sexual well-being is connected to general health, nurses address it to support the whole patient across different life stages. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h1)

question: How long does standard multidrug therapy (MDT) last for multibacillary leprosy?

options.A: Twelve to twenty-four months
options.B: Five years or lifelong
options.C: Exactly six months
options.D: Two to four weeks

explanation: Correct! Multibacillary cases need a longer treatment stretch, usually 12 to 24 months, to clear the heavy germ load.

question: At what point during your shift should you separate hospital waste?

options.A: Only when the local sanitation truck arrives
options.B: During final transport outside the hospital gates
options.C: After all waste is mixed together in the utility room
options.D: At the exact moment and place of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right at the bedside as you create it! Waiting until later increases the risk of mistakes and accidental injuries.

question: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually take place?

options.A: Body of the uterus
options.B: Cervical canal
options.C: Ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Ovarian cortex

explanation: Spot on! The ampulla is the wider section of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg love to finally meet and fuse.

question: What is an important food safety habit a nurse should teach families to prevent cross-contamination?

options.A: Reusing cooking oil indefinitely without filtering it
options.B: Keeping raw foods and cooked foods strictly separated
options.C: Washing all kitchen knives with cold water only
options.D: Storing all fresh vegetables inside closed plastic bags in the sun

explanation: Always keep raw meats away from ready-to-eat meals so harmful bacteria don't hitch a ride onto your food.

question: Why are nurses often considered the central hub of the healthcare team?

options.A: They spend the most continuous time at the patient bedside
options.B: They make all the final diagnoses for hospital admissions
options.C: They hold the legal authority to hire and fire doctors
options.D: They control the entire hospital financial budget

explanation: That's right! Because nurses are right there by the bedside around the clock, we are usually the first to notice changes and connect all the other team members.

question: What is the primary goal of triage in an emergency department?

options.A: To sort patients based on the severity of their condition
options.B: To assign a private room to every arriving patient
options.C: To collect insurance and billing information promptly
options.D: To discharge patients who have minor complaints quickly

explanation: Triage allows nurses to prioritize care so that the most critically ill or injured patients receive immediate attention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h1)

question: Who is the main client for a community health nurse?

options.A: The entire community or population
options.B: Only children under five years old
options.C: Patients admitted to the surgical ward
options.D: Physicians working in rural clinics

explanation: You've got this! While ward nurses care for one patient at a time, community health nurses look out for whole neighborhoods and populations.

question: Which nursing practice is widely known as the most effective way to stop infections from spreading in hospitals?

options.A: Painting hospital walls with bright colors
options.B: Regular and thorough hand hygiene
options.C: Replacing all cotton uniforms with nylon
options.D: Closing the outpatient department daily at noon

explanation: Spot on! Simple, consistent handwashing remains our absolute best defense against spreading healthcare-associated infections.

question: What is a major advantage of using questionnaires in nursing research?

options.A: They guarantee a 100 percent response rate from participants
options.B: They can efficiently gather data from large numbers of people
options.C: They completely eliminate the possibility of human bias
options.D: They allow researchers to perform deep physical exams

explanation: Questionnaires can be distributed widely via mail or the internet, making it easy to collect data from large populations quickly. Excellent job!

question: What is a tricky downside of pie charts when values are very close to each other?

options.A: Statistical software blocks their creation
options.B: They require complex mathematical formulas to read
options.C: They cannot display percentages greater than 50
options.D: The human eye struggles to compare slice sizes accurately

explanation: Correct! It's genuinely hard for our eyes to tell the difference between two slices that look almost the same size.

question: Why is teaching family caregivers a key part of subacute discharge planning?

options.A: It allows family members to legally substitute for trained nurses
options.B: It removes the need for any follow-up visits with primary doctors
options.C: It ensures the facility receives additional government funding
options.D: It prepares them to safely manage medications and care tasks at home

explanation: You nailed it. Equipping family caregivers prevents slip-ups and keeps the patient from bouncing back to the hospital.

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To sweep over the ovary and catch the released egg
options.B: To push sperm upward into the uterine cavity
options.C: To attach the ovary firmly to the pelvic wall
options.D: To secrete hormones that trigger monthly ovulation

explanation: The finger-like fimbriae use gentle sweeping movements to guide the newly released egg into the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to understand basic economic trends?

options.A: Economic trends directly affect hospital funding and resources
options.B: Nurses must calculate national tax allocations
options.C: Clinical diagnoses depend on inflation rates
options.D: Hospital management requires nurses to trade stocks

explanation: Great question! National economic performance dictates government budgets, which trickle down to hospital supplies, staffing, and facility maintenance.

question: Which of the following must be avoided when writing clinical notes in a client file?

options.A: Personal opinions, biases, or derogatory comments about the client
options.B: Exact dates and times of medication administration
options.C: Objective measurements like blood pressure and weight
options.D: The signature and professional rank of the attending nurse

explanation: Clinical records must remain professional and objective, avoiding judgmental language or subjective personal opinions about the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h7)

question: A 10-week-old baby is brought for immunizations, but currently has a high fever and a bad cough. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the child straight to surgery for a diagnostic blood test
options.B: Defer the immunizations temporarily until the acute illness resolves
options.C: Administer all scheduled vaccines immediately regardless of the fever
options.D: Permanently ban the child from receiving any future vaccines

explanation: When a child is acutely sick with a high fever, it's wise to hold off (defer) the shots until they feel better so symptoms don't get confused.

question: When scientific research is described as 'empirical', what does that mean?

options.A: It is based on direct observation and real-world data
options.B: It focuses only on historical events from the past
options.C: It changes every time a new person reads the report
options.D: It relies entirely on the personal opinion of the researcher

explanation: Well done! Empirical simply means it is built on tangible evidence and real-world observations, not just guesses.

question: When should a nurse consider referring a psychiatric client to a sheltered workshop?

options.A: When the client is experiencing an acute, violent psychotic episode
options.B: When the client is medically stable but lacks skills for open jobs
options.C: When the client refuses to take any prescribed medications
options.D: When the client demands discharge against medical advice

explanation: Referral works best when acute symptoms are well-managed and the client is ready for gentle rehabilitation. Excellent nursing judgment!

question: Who usually passes down nutritional taboos in traditional communities?

options.A: Modern clinical dietitians and nurses
options.B: Community elders and cultural leaders
options.C: Local government agricultural officers
options.D: International health organization workers

explanation: Generational beliefs and food rules are typically preserved and taught by the older members and leaders of the community.

question: Why is it tricky to use a stethoscope when a patient is lying on a very soft home bed?

options.A: Patients usually fall asleep immediately upon lying down on them.
options.B: Soft mattresses absorb all the sound waves from the stethoscope.
options.C: It makes proper patient positioning and organ assessment difficult.
options.D: Soft beds prevent the nurse from checking the patient's radial pulse.

explanation: Well done! A soft, unsupportive bed makes it hard to keep the correct posture needed to properly listen to the chest and tummy.

question: What is the main purpose of placing electrode pads on a patient's chest for cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To capture the electrical activity and heart rhythm
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient warm during cold hospital nights
options.D: To deliver mild electric shocks to warm the skin

explanation: Electrodes pick up the heart's electrical impulses and display them as a waveform on the screen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: How do modern informatics tools make communication between different healthcare pros much easier?

options.A: By providing a centralized digital hub for notes, labs, and orders
options.B: By allowing patients to directly alter their medication schedules
options.C: By automatically calling doctors whenever a vital sign changes
options.D: By replacing all face-to-face shift change meetings entirely

explanation: Spot on! Having one central digital chart means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists are all looking at the exact same page, reducing miscommunication on the ward.

question: A patient with heart failure needs an IV infusion. What is your most important pre-infusion check?

options.A: Choosing a vein located in the dominant hand for comfort
options.B: Selecting the largest gauge needle available for rapid infusion
options.C: Warming the intravenous fluid bag to body temperature first
options.D: Listening to the client's lung sounds and checking baseline vital signs

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Heart failure patients struggle to handle extra fluid. Checking their lungs and vitals first gives you a baseline so you can catch early signs of fluid overload.

question: Why is the triage nurse's job considered to carry big legal responsibilities?

options.A: A missed critical symptom during the initial sort can cause severe patient harm
options.B: Hospital insurance does not cover mistakes made outside the ward
options.C: Triage nurses must personally pay for any medication ordered at the desk
options.D: The nurse is legally required to diagnose every disease on arrival

explanation: Because triage is the very first stop, catching critical symptoms early protects the patient and keeps your clinical practice safe.

question: Why is giving injections straight into the heart a last resort in today's hospitals?

options.A: It requires special oral preparation before injection
options.B: It takes too long for the medication to reach the brain
options.C: It can only be performed by a pharmacist in a laboratory
options.D: It carries severe risks of heart damage and safer routes usually work

explanation: Poking the heart muscle can cause serious bleeding and injury. That's why nurses and doctors always try IV or bone (intraosseous) lines first!

question: Why is it important to teach digital health topics in nursing school?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside clinical practice with computer gaming
options.B: To prepare student nurses for modern virtual communication and digital care delivery
options.C: To ensure students never have to care for physical patients in wards
options.D: To teach students how to repair broken telephone network towers

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is changing fast. Learning digital health early equips you with the skills you need for modern nursing practice.

question: Why do we call Ebola a zoonotic disease?

options.A: It spreads exclusively among wild animals in the forest
options.B: It can only be transmitted through contaminated water
options.C: It mutates rapidly inside human respiratory tracts
options.D: It originates in animals and spreads to humans

explanation: You got it! 'Zoonotic' simply means an infection that jumps from animals to humans. Easy peasy!

question: Heparin is a common drug used to prevent blood clots. Where is it traditionally sourced from?

options.A: Avian egg membrane
options.B: Equine blood plasma
options.C: Bovine pancreatic tissue
options.D: Porcine intestinal mucosa

explanation: Heparin is safely extracted from the mucosal lining of pig (porcine) intestines for its wonderful blood-thinning power.

question: What does a nurse check when assessing normal uterine involution during a postnatal home visit?

options.A: The complete absence of lochia discharge after twenty-four hours
options.B: The permanent softening of the abdominal wall muscles
options.C: The gradual decrease in the size and height of the uterus
options.D: The rapid increase in maternal body weight

explanation: Involution is the normal process where the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size, felt as a steadily lowering fundal height. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is capitation in the context of HMO operations?

options.A: A cash penalty paid by patients who miss clinic appointments
options.B: A special tax collected from hospital workers
options.C: A fixed regular payment per head made to a primary provider
options.D: The total cost of building a new pharmacy

explanation: Capitation means 'per head,' where the clinic receives a set amount monthly for every registered member, absorbing the risk if they fall sick or gaining if they stay healthy. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a health insurance scheme?

options.A: To pool financial risks and protect people from high out-of-pocket costs
options.B: To ensure that doctors receive higher salaries than other workers
options.C: To provide free luxury accommodation for all hospitalized patients
options.D: To eliminate the need for government funding in hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Insurance pools money from many people so that when someone falls sick, they don't get completely wiped out financially by medical bills.

question: What are the three core elements that make up Evidence-Based Practice (EBP)?

options.A: Financial cost, administrative goals, and staff availability
options.B: Hospital policy, doctor orders, and nursing intuition
options.C: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.D: Textbook theory, peer pressure, and trial-and-error

explanation: Brilliant! EBP is a sweet spot that combines what science proves, what your clinical skills tell you, and what the patient actually prefers.

question: What is the tongue's main job right at the start of swallowing food?

options.A: Producing digestive enzymes to break down starches
options.B: Sealing off the nasopharynx to prevent nasal regurgitation
options.C: Pushing the food bolus backward against the hard palate
options.D: Opening the upper esophageal sphincter mechanically

explanation: When you swallow, your tongue acts like a natural spatula, pressing food up and back toward your throat.

question: Why must a hospital conduct manpower planning before hiring new nurses?

options.A: To match the number of available staff with patient care needs
options.B: To decide which brand of uniforms the nursing staff will wear
options.C: To reduce the basic monthly salary of existing nursing staff
options.D: To fulfill government rules without needing actual hospital data

explanation: Manpower planning is just figuring out how many hands we actually need on deck so we don't end up severely understaffed or wasting money.

question: What is the main goal of nursing data integration?

options.A: Lowering the financial cost of hospital building maintenance
options.B: Replacing all human nurses with automated computer programs
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital beds needed
options.D: Bringing patient information together into a single view

explanation: You've got this! Data integration simply means gathering scattered patient details from different places so you can see the whole picture in one spot. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why must a public health nurse look beyond single patients when studying a community?

options.A: To ensure that doctors do not interfere with community nursing duties
options.B: So that the nurse can prescribe drugs without a medical doctor present
options.C: To spot wider patterns of disease linked to shared environmental or economic factors
options.D: Because individual hospital records are completely useless for public health

explanation: Looking at the bigger picture reveals systemic issues affecting the whole population, not just isolated cases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h1)

question: Which natural hazard displaces thousands of people every year in Nigerian coastal and river areas?

options.A: Tidal tsunamis
options.B: Seasonal flooding
options.C: Volcanic eruptions
options.D: Severe blizzards

explanation: Exactly! Heavy seasonal rains often overflow river banks, causing widespread displacement in many parts of Nigeria.

question: Why is priority setting necessary during community mobilisation?

options.A: Resources are limited, so the community must focus on the most pressing problem
options.B: It stops people from talking during community meetings
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to work on more than two diseases at a time
options.D: The government requires every village to solve exactly one problem per year

explanation: Because time, money, and materials are limited, communities must rank their problems and tackle the most urgent ones first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: The brand name of soap used for their bath
options.B: The patient's favorite food and religious beliefs
options.C: The cost of the hospital bed and your home address
options.D: Joints exercised, how the patient tolerated it, and any unusual findings

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing notes always focus on the clinical facts: what you moved, how they reacted, and anything out of the ordinary.

question: During which step of the PDSA cycle does a nurse compare the actual results of a test against what they predicted would happen?

options.A: Study
options.B: Act
options.C: Plan
options.D: Do

explanation: In the 'Study' phase, you pause to look at the data and check: 'Did our test work out the way we thought it would?'

question: What is a likely result of poor onboarding and weak orientation programs?

options.A: Greater trust between doctors and nurses
options.B: Lower hospital spending on medical supplies
options.C: Faster completion of daily ward chores
options.D: Higher rates of early resignation among new staff

explanation: When new nurses feel unsupported and overwhelmed, they are much more likely to leave the facility quickly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: What are the three core action steps when giving Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

options.A: Look, Listen, Link
options.B: Calm, Medicate, Refer
options.C: Assess, Diagnose, Treat
options.D: Examine, Probe, Analyze

explanation: Easy to remember! PFA is all about three simple steps: Look around, Listen actively, and Link the person to help or their support system.

question: Which part of the spinal cord gives rise to the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Lumbar and sacral region
options.B: Craniosacral region
options.C: Thoracolumbar region
options.D: Cervical region only

explanation: Sympathetic fibers emerge from the chest (thoracic) and upper lower-back (lumbar) areas of the spine. That's why we call it the thoracolumbar outflow!

question: In the chain of infection, what is considered the final link?

options.A: The portal of exit
options.B: The reservoir of infection
options.C: The susceptible host
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: You've got this! The chain ends with the susceptible host—that's a person who doesn't have enough immunity to fight off the germ.

question: What is the best way to describe mental health in nursing?

options.A: Having an intelligence score far above the average
options.B: The total absence of any psychological distress or worry
options.C: A state of complete emotional and physical numbness
options.D: A state of well-being where a person can cope with normal stress

explanation: Mental health isn't just about never feeling sad or stressed. It's about having the coping skills to handle everyday pressures, work productively, and contribute to your community. You're doing great!

question: Before giving a drug, you use a bedside tool to scan both the patient's wristband and the medication. What is this safety tool called?

options.A: Automated vital sign tracking
options.B: Bar Code Medication Administration
options.C: Clinical Decision Support Systems
options.D: Electronic Health Record auditing

explanation: Brilliant! Bar Code Medication Administration (BCMA) is your trusty safety net at the bedside, making sure the right patient gets the right drug, dose, and route every single time.

question: Why do researchers use random assignment when setting up a clinical study?

options.A: To lower the cost of buying hospital drugs
options.B: To guarantee the study applies to the whole world
options.C: To finish the study as quickly as possible
options.D: To balance out differences between patients and protect internal validity

explanation: Randomly putting patients into groups helps ensure both groups start off similar, so we know the treatment—not patient differences—made the change.

question: Severe sleep deprivation affects a nurse's reaction time and judgment similarly to which of the following?

options.A: Alcohol intoxication
options.B: A mild fever
options.C: Hyperglycemic shock
options.D: Caffeine overdose

explanation: It sounds shocking, but studies show that going too long without sleep messes with your brain just as much as being legally drunk. Rest is vital!

question: What is the big advantage of an enterprise EHR system in a large health network?

options.A: It connects multiple hospitals and clinics into a single shared database
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to document patient assessments
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors in outpatient clinics
options.D: It automatically lowers the cost of prescription drugs for patients

explanation: Correct! Enterprise systems tie various hospitals and clinics together so patient files travel smoothly across the whole network.

question: Which physical finding shows a patient has a very full, distended bladder?

options.A: A firm, rounded swelling above the pubic bone that sounds dull when tapped
options.B: Severe swelling and redness around the external genitalia
options.C: A soft, sunken abdomen that is completely silent to stethoscope listening
options.D: Sharp pain radiating from the flank down to the groin area

explanation: A full bladder feels like a firm bump just above the pubic bone, and fluid makes a dull sound when you tap on it. Assessment skills unlocked!

question: An elderly client is returning home after hip surgery. What is the best safety upgrade to make in their bathroom?

options.A: Placing a thick cloth rug directly on the slippery wet floor
options.B: Installing grab bars near the toilet and inside the shower
options.C: Removing the bathroom door to allow faster nursing access
options.D: Turning off bathroom lights at night to encourage rest

explanation: You got it! Bathrooms are wet and slick—grab bars give patients the extra support they need during transfers to prevent nasty falls. Great nursing judgment!

question: A client returns to the ward after having a TURBT (transurethral resection of a bladder tumor). What is your priority nursing check?

options.A: Assessing for bilateral swelling of the lower leg joints
options.B: Checking for sudden changes in visual acuity and hearing
options.C: Monitoring urinary output and watching for bleeding
options.D: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels every two hours

explanation: After bladder surgery, keeping a close eye on their urine through the catheter is vital. We watch for bright red blood or clots so we can catch any bleeding early!

question: What is 'alert fatigue' when nurses deal with hospital computers?

options.A: Experiencing physical exhaustion from working long night shifts on a computer
options.B: Growing tired of attending mandatory computer training classes every year
options.C: Feeling overwhelmed by the bright display screens used in hospital monitors
options.D: Becoming desensitized to frequent warning pop-ups and ignoring important prompts

explanation: When computers give too many minor warnings all day, nurses start ignoring them—which can be dangerous if a real emergency alert pops up! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which breathing condition is most commonly treated with a steam tent?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Croup
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! Croup causes that classic barking cough, and warm, moist air is one of the best ways to bring relief.

question: A student nurse notices a wrong drug dose written by a senior doctor, but stays quiet because she is scared of shouting. What is missing in this team?

options.A: Lack of psychological safety
options.B: Poor physical infrastructure of the ward
options.C: Inadequate clinical pharmacology knowledge
options.D: Absence of basic hospital policies

explanation: Spot on! When people stay silent about dangerous situations out of fear, it shows the team lacks psychological safety.

question: Which instrument is most commonly used for safe uterine evacuation during PAC procedures?

options.A: Disposable plastic speculum
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) kit
options.C: Rigid metal obstetric forceps
options.D: Standard surgical scalpel

explanation: MVA kits use a gentle suction created by a handheld syringe to empty the uterus safely and effectively with minimal trauma to the patient.

question: What triggers the strong inflammatory flare-up called the Mazzotti reaction during parasite treatment?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the plastic pill capsule
options.B: Sudden dehydration caused by lack of drinking water
options.C: Direct toxic injury to human liver cells by the drug
options.D: The rapid release of proteins from dying microfilariae

explanation: You're doing great! When masses of tiny parasites die off all at once, releasing their proteins into the blood, it sparks a strong immune reaction.

question: Why are bedside nurses usually the best people to spot where clinical changes are needed?

options.A: They spend most of their shift working in the hospital administrative offices
options.B: They dictate national health policies and regulatory frameworks
options.C: They have final authority over hospital budget allocations
options.D: They experience daily workflows and spot operational bottlenecks firsthand

explanation: You are right at the bedside every day, so you see firsthand what slows things down or causes delays for patients. Who knows the ward better than you?

question: When is a nursing research topic considered to lack practical value?

options.A: If it fails to include at least five different hospitals
options.B: If it uses complex laboratory equipment
options.C: If it fails to change or improve current clinical practice
options.D: If it generates millions of naira in profit

explanation: If the findings don't help us care for patients better at the bedside, the study misses the main point of nursing research.

question: Why is a full, holistic health assessment important when looking at a gifted child?

options.A: To measure precise intelligence quotients for legal classification
options.B: To ensure the child skips multiple grades in primary school
options.C: To catch hidden issues like underachievement and emotional distress
options.D: To diagnose physical growth abnormalities caused by high intellect

explanation: Brilliant grades can hide a lot of stress! A holistic check helps nurses spot hidden emotional struggles that high intelligence might mask. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: Which common side effect is often linked to ACE inhibitors like lisinopril?

options.A: A persistent dry cough
options.B: Extreme darkening of the urine
options.C: Severe yellowing of the eyes
options.D: Uncontrollable muscle twitching

explanation: You nailed it! ACE inhibitors can cause a buildup in the lungs that leads to a nagging, dry cough for some patients.

question: Which pillar of safe motherhood focuses on checking on the mother and baby right after childbirth?

options.A: Family planning
options.B: Obstetric care
options.C: Antenatal care
options.D: Postnatal care

explanation: Well done! Postnatal care happens after delivery to make sure both mother and baby are recovering smoothly.

question: What is a very important safety step when caring for an elderly patient who just started a tranquilizer?

options.A: Checking blood glucose levels every two hours
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent nighttime urination
options.C: Encouraging immediate participation in heavy physical exercise
options.D: Implementing strict fall precautions due to sedation and dizziness

explanation: Sedatives make older adults feel dizzy and unsteady on their feet, so keeping them safe from accidental falls is a top nursing priority!

question: What happens when communication breaks down during a disaster response?

options.A: The federal government automatically increases funding for local clinics
options.B: International aid organizations decide to withdraw completely from the region
options.C: Rescue efforts stall and resources are wasted due to lack of coordination
options.D: Community members become more resilient against future emergencies

explanation: Good communication is everything! Without it, teams duplicate work or miss sending help to where it's needed most.

question: What is the main job of a Quality Assurance (QA) Committee in a hospital?

options.A: Hiring and firing clinical staff members
options.B: Managing the hospital budget and staff salaries
options.C: Checking and improving the standard of patient care
options.D: Buying new medical equipment for the wards

explanation: You got this! A QA committee is basically the hospital's safety and quality champion, making sure patients get the best care possible.

question: Which of these organs is found in the upper belly (abdominal) part of the abdominopelvic cavity?

options.A: Brain
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Urinary bladder
options.D: Stomach

explanation: Your stomach hangs out in the upper tummy area, while your bladder is tucked way down in the pelvis.

question: Why do healthcare workers usually resist new changes in the workplace?

options.A: Laziness and a general refusal to work hard
options.B: A normal defense mechanism against the unknown
options.C: An inadequate level of basic clinical training
options.D: A deliberate attempt to sabotage patient safety

explanation: You're doing great! Resistance isn't about being lazy—it's just a natural human reaction when our daily routine gets shaken up by the unknown.

question: What do we mean by the 'second victim' in healthcare?

options.A: The family members who witness a patient's decline
options.B: The secondary patient sharing a room with the affected individual
options.C: The healthcare professionals who experience emotional trauma after an error
options.D: The hospital institution that faces lawsuits and financial fines

explanation: The 'second victim' is the nurse or doctor who suffers deep emotional pain and stress after being involved in an unexpected patient incident.

question: What does the principle of equity mean in mental health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring vulnerable groups have fair access to support
options.B: Allowing only community leaders to make decisions
options.C: Giving the exact same treatment to every single person
options.D: Making sure rich people pay for poor people's drugs

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness and making sure that those who face the greatest disadvantages receive the resources they need to thrive. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling vector-borne diseases like malaria in a community?

options.A: Washing hospital floors with scented detergent twice a day
options.B: Eliminating stagnant water breeding sites and using bed nets
options.C: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy adult
options.D: Replacing all plastic medical equipment with stainless steel

explanation: Vector control targets the insects that transmit parasites by destroying their breeding grounds and preventing bites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h7)

question: How does economic abuse primarily trap a victim in an abusive relationship?

options.A: By encouraging the victim to spend money without keeping financial records
options.B: By removing the financial resources needed to live independently and leave
options.C: By rewarding the victim with gifts only when they obey household rules
options.D: By forcing the victim to spend all their savings on expensive medical bills

explanation: Controlling all money and stopping the victim from working makes it nearly impossible for them to afford housing or food on their own. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h5)

question: What is an effective strategy to improve nutritional intake in an older adult with poor appetite?

options.A: Waiting until the patient asks for food once a day
options.B: Serving small, nutrient-dense meals more frequently
options.C: Removing all favorite cultural foods from the diet
options.D: Forcing the patient to finish three large meals daily

explanation: Smaller meals are less overwhelming for seniors with low appetite, and making them nutrient-dense ensures they still get enough calories and vitamins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h4)

question: A family caregiver is exhausted and needs a short break to run errands. Which hospice team member is best suited to sit with the patient during this time?

options.A: A medical social worker
options.B: A registered nurse
options.C: A hospice volunteer
options.D: A certified nursing assistant

explanation: Volunteers frequently provide companionship and respite care, giving family caregivers time away to rest or attend to personal errands. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h4)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements to women in early pregnancy?

options.A: To accelerate infant tooth eruption
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy helps protect the baby's developing brain and spinal cord. Super important vitamin!

question: Along with classic symptoms, what random blood sugar level usually points toward diabetes?

options.A: 200 mg/dL or higher
options.B: 120 to 139 mg/dL
options.C: 90 to 110 mg/dL
options.D: 50 to 70 mg/dL

explanation: An RBS reading of 200 mg/dL or more, paired with signs like extreme thirst and frequent urination, is a strong red flag for diabetes.

question: What is the fastest way to crash and bankrupt a working Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Conducting regular monthly stock counts of all tablets
options.B: Giving out large quantities of medicines on uncontrolled credit
options.C: Keeping the pharmacy store clean, dry, and well-ventilated
options.D: Buying drugs in large bulk quantities directly from manufacturers

explanation: You nailed it! If people take drugs on credit and never pay back, the cash never returns to buy new stock, and the fund collapses.

question: What is the name of the rounded fatty pad that sits right over the pubic bone?

options.A: The labia majora
options.B: The clitoral hood
options.C: The perineum
options.D: The mons pubis

explanation: Great job! The mons pubis is that cushioned, fatty mound over the pubic bone that protects the area underneath.

question: How does proper health funding positively impact the wider national economy?

options.A: It reduces worker absenteeism and boosts productivity
options.B: It eliminates the need for any private sector businesses
options.C: It forces manufacturing companies to close down
options.D: It increases the amount of money spent on treating epidemics

explanation: Healthy citizens miss fewer days of work or school, leading to higher overall economic productivity for the nation. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h6)

question: When designing public health education, what does 'acceptability' mean?

options.A: Whether the target community welcomes and relates to the educational tool
options.B: Whether the government health ministry has stamped it with an official seal
options.C: How many pages of text the target population is willing to read
options.D: How cheaply the printing press can manufacture the paper flyers

explanation: Acceptability is all about whether the community feels comfortable with the material and feels it matches their personal values and beliefs.

question: What are the three main categories in the biopsychosocial model?

options.A: Genetics, environment, and medication
options.B: Biological, psychological, and social factors
options.C: Emotional, behavioral, and cultural traits
options.D: Physical, spiritual, and financial factors

explanation: The biopsychosocial model organizes the causes of mental illness into three core dimensions: biological, psychological, and social. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why can regular hospital IV pumps sometimes cause trouble during a flight?

options.A: Air pressure causes the IV tubing to melt
options.B: Vibration and pressure changes can affect pump accuracy
options.C: Infusion pumps require constant connection to plumbing
options.D: Hospital pumps are too quiet to hear over the engines

explanation: You're doing great! Engine vibrations and shifts in cabin air pressure can mess with standard pumps, so flight nurses use specially calibrated equipment.

question: Which common everyday drink should patients with anxiety and phobias cut back on because it triggers jitters and a fast heart rate?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Caffeine
options.C: Complex carbohydrates
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Caffeine is a stimulant. Too much coffee or energy drink can easily mimic or worsen panic symptoms like a racing pulse and shaky hands.

question: What is the main nutritional gift that cereal grains like rice, maize, and guinea corn give our bodies?

options.A: Vitamin B12 for nerve function
options.B: Complete animal protein profiles
options.C: Complex carbohydrates for energy
options.D: High amounts of dietary cholesterol

explanation: Awesome! Cereals are our main energy staples, loaded with complex carbs to keep us moving through long ward shifts and lectures.

question: When a registered nurse delegates a task to a junior colleague, who remains ultimately accountable?

options.A: The hospital chief medical director
options.B: The registered nurse who delegated the task
options.C: The junior staff member who performed the task
options.D: The patient's family members

explanation: Delegating a task shares the physical work, but as the RN, you keep the overall accountability to ensure it was done safely.

question: Why does the healthcare team do a home assessment before a patient is discharged?

options.A: It helps identify physical barriers like stairs or narrow doors that could cause falls or limit mobility
options.B: It replaces the need for physical therapy sessions in the clinic
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the client no longer needs any assistance
options.D: It allows the hospital to bill the client for interior decorating services

explanation: Checking the home early helps spot hazards like steps or narrow doors so ramps or rails can be fitted before the patient arrives. Safety first!

question: Why can't you rely solely on looking at a vaccine to know if heat has ruined it?

options.A: Heat damage does not change the physical appearance of the liquid
options.B: Vaccines change color only when exposed to freezing temperatures
options.C: Expired vaccines always look completely normal to the naked eye
options.D: Modern glass vials are coated with special heat-reflective paint

explanation: Most heat-damaged vaccines look totally normal! That's why temperature logs and Vaccine Vial Monitors (VVMs) are our best friends.

question: What is the main physiological purpose of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile salts to help break down dietary fats
options.B: Absorbing remaining water and compacting indigestible waste
options.C: Digesting complex proteins into single amino acids
options.D: Secreting hydrochloric acid to kill swallowed bacteria

explanation: By the time food residue gets to the colon, most nutrients are already gone. The large intestine's main task is to suck back the water and turn waste into solid stool.

question: Why must disaster nurses actively watch out for compassion fatigue and practice self-care?

options.A: Patients will lose respect for nurses who show emotion
options.B: Nurses are immune to stress if they work fast enough
options.C: Hospital managers require daily wellness logs from every nurse
options.D: Prolonged exposure to trauma can lead to severe emotional burnout

explanation: So true! Seeing constant suffering wears down even the strongest nurses. Taking care of your own mental health keeps you and your patients safe.

question: Why do nurses always warn patients with bleeding problems to stay away from everyday painkillers like ibuprofen?

options.A: NSAIDs increase blood pressure to dangerous levels and trigger acute strokes
options.B: NSAIDs instantly destroy all stored vitamin K reserves located inside the liver
options.C: NSAIDs negatively interfere with normal platelet aggregation and increase bleeding risks
options.D: NSAIDs cause the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells permanently

explanation: Medications like ibuprofen and aspirin get in the way of platelets sticking together, making it much harder for your body to stop any bleeding.

question: What happens when a person suffers severe damage to their hippocampus?

options.A: They lose the ability to feel physical pain
options.B: They experience paralysis in their lower limbs
options.C: They forget all their childhood memories
options.D: They can no longer form new long-term memories

explanation: You nailed it! The hippocampus is needed to lock in new experiences into long-term storage, so damage makes forming new memories very difficult.

question: What is the main purpose of vaccinating animals on a large scale in public health?

options.A: To cure animals that are already showing severe clinical signs of illness
options.B: To create a protective barrier that stops pathogens from spreading to humans
options.C: To increase the market weight and commercial value of livestock herds
options.D: To replace human vaccination schedules with veterinary immunization protocols

explanation: Exactly! Vaccinating animals keeps them healthy and stops zoonotic diseases from jumping over to humans.

question: What is the main job of the pneumotaxic center in the pons?

options.A: Controlling fine motor skills in the hands
options.B: Controlling the transition between inhalation and exhalation
options.C: Processing visual images from the retina
options.D: Regulating conscious thought processes

explanation: Think of the pneumotaxic center as a smooth rhythm controller for breathing, helping you switch easily between breathing in and breathing out.

question: What is the final, essential step when using evaluation data for quality improvement?

options.A: Stopping all routine data collection for the next year
options.B: Punishing staff members whose coverage rates are low
options.C: Filing the completed assessment reports in a locked cabinet
options.D: Implementing corrective actions based on the findings

explanation: Data collection is only useful if we act on it! We must turn our findings into practical changes to improve care for children.

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of psychiatric follow-up care?

options.A: Isolating the patient from their family and community
options.B: Focusing solely on physical injuries rather than mood
options.C: Preventing relapse and maintaining symptom stability
options.D: Encouraging the patient to stop taking all medications

explanation: Keeping symptoms stable and preventing a return of acute illness is a central objective of ongoing mental health visits. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the single most important step in managing hospital waste safely?

options.A: Segregation
options.B: Compacting
options.C: Exporting
options.D: Incineration

explanation: Sorting or segregating your waste right at the bedside is key! If you separate things correctly from the start, every step that follows becomes much safer and easier.

question: Why must data collection instruments be valid and reliable in cross-sectional research?

options.A: To make sure patients take their medications on time
options.B: To guarantee that the study takes at least five years to finish
options.C: To prevent the researcher from having to use statistics
options.D: To ensure the measurements are accurate and consistent

explanation: Validity and reliability simply mean your measuring tool actually tests what it's supposed to, and gives steady results every time.

question: Why are older adults at such a high risk for becoming dehydrated?

options.A: They are physically unable to swallow any liquids
options.B: Doctors usually restrict them from drinking fluids
options.C: They have a diminished sense of thirst as they age
options.D: Their bodies require less water than children do

explanation: The natural aging process can dull the body's thirst trigger, meaning seniors often just don't feel thirsty even when their bodies desperately need water.

question: What type of cells make up the inner part of the adrenal gland (adrenal medulla), and where do they come from?

options.A: C cells derived from the embryonic pharyngeal pouches
options.B: Chromaffin cells, which are modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons
options.C: Epithelial cells arranged in hollow spherical follicles containing colloid
options.D: Follicular cells that synthesize and store mineralocorticoids

explanation: The adrenal medulla is unique! Its chromaffin cells are basically modified nerve cells that release adrenaline straight into your blood during a fight-or-flight moment.

question: What exactly is a 'windshield survey' in community health nursing?

options.A: A formal written examination taken by student nurses before clinical rotation
options.B: An aerial drone photography mapping of agricultural farm yields
options.C: A laboratory test measuring the air pollution levels in a factory zone
options.D: An observational walk or drive through a community to note living conditions

explanation: Think of a windshield survey as a clinical sightseeing trip! You drive or walk through the neighborhood, keeping your eyes open to observe housing, waste disposal, and general everyday life.

question: What is the main goal of a sheltered workshop for clients?

options.A: Providing permanent long-term housing
options.B: Maximizing company profit margins
options.C: Replacing traditional hospital care entirely
options.D: Rehabilitation and skill building

explanation: Sheltered workshops are designed to help clients recover and learn useful skills in a safe, supportive space rather than focusing on business profits. You've got this!

question: Which of the following best describes raw, unorganized facts without context?

options.A: Knowledge
options.B: Wisdom
options.C: Information
options.D: Data

explanation: Data represents the raw, isolated facts, such as a single vital sign measurement, before they are processed or given context. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the very first piece of PPE a nurse should put on when donning for isolation care?

options.A: The gloves
options.B: The gown
options.C: The face mask
options.D: The eye goggles

question: Which of these is a key step for nursing leaders building a Just Culture?

options.A: Eliminating all clinical guidelines so nurses can practice purely on intuition
options.B: Keeping incident reports strictly secret from frontline nursing staff
options.C: Punishing every single reported error to stop future carelessness
options.D: Ensuring hospital policies are fair and applied consistently across departments

explanation: Fairness and consistency build the trust needed to keep a Just Culture thriving in any hospital.

question: What is the main job of an occupational therapist in a rehab team?

options.A: Managing hospital financial budgets and payroll
options.B: Helping patients master fine motor skills and daily activities
options.C: Prescribing pharmaceutical drugs for acute infections
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries on fractured bones

explanation: Correct! Occupational therapists focus on helping people get back to daily essentials like eating, dressing, bathing, and working.

question: Which tool do nurses commonly use to check a patient's ability to handle daily activities?

options.A: Braden Pressure Scale
options.B: Katz Index of Independence
options.C: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.D: Apgar Scoring System

explanation: You got it! The Katz Index is the go-to tool for checking how well a person manages everyday tasks on their own.

question: A patient has a BMI of 32.5. How is this classified?

options.A: Normal weight
options.B: Overweight
options.C: Obesity
options.D: Underweight

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a continuous supply of affordable essential drugs
options.B: To provide free medical care to all indigent citizens
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and buildings
options.D: To generate heavy profits for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF as a self-sustaining cycle. Its main job is to make sure essential drugs never run out in the hospital pharmacy, so patients can always get what they need at a fair price!

question: Why does poor fetal growth (intrauterine growth restriction) happen more often in teenage mums?

options.A: The young mother's body and the placenta compete for limited nutrients
options.B: Fetal growth is naturally faster when the mother is under eighteen
options.C: Adolescents consume too many synthetic vitamins during gestation
options.D: The amniotic fluid volume increases excessively and crushes the fetus

explanation: Since a teenager is still growing herself, her body uses up nutrients that the baby desperately needs for proper growth.

question: What is the primary neurotransmitter blocked by anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Norepinephrine
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: Anticholinergic drugs specifically target and block acetylcholine receptors in the nervous system. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h1)

question: A patient receives a newly confirmed HIV-positive result during post-test counselling and appears visibly shaken. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Scold the patient for engaging in risky lifestyle behaviors
options.B: Demand the names and addresses of all past sexual partners
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately to avoid crowding the clinic
options.D: Provide psychological first aid and assess immediate safety risks

question: How many general objectives should a standard nursing research proposal have?

options.A: Only one
options.B: As many as the researcher wants

explanation: Keep it focused! A study generally centers around one single overarching goal, meaning you only need one general objective. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which of these best describes for-profit healthcare providers?

options.A: They are strictly owned and managed by local government councils
options.B: They operate as commercial businesses aiming to generate financial returns
options.C: They offer free medical services to every member of the public
options.D: They rely exclusively on volunteer staff and donated medical supplies

question: Which of these is a normal mental response when someone is in acute grief?

options.A: Total inability to recognize family members forever
options.B: Forgetfulness and poor concentration
options.C: Advanced intellectual enhancement
options.D: Permanent memory loss from brain damage

explanation: Mental fog and trouble focusing are totally normal temporary reactions to high emotional stress. You're doing great!

question: Why is it best to combine mass media with face-to-face counselling in health campaigns?

options.A: Mass media is always more accurate than anything a nurse can say in person
options.B: Government regulations require both methods to be used simultaneously
options.C: Face-to-face counselling is too expensive to use unless mass media has failed
options.D: Mass media reaches many people quickly, while face-to-face counselling allows personal questions

explanation: Radio and posters help spread the word far and wide fast, but sitting down to talk allows patients to ask questions and clear up personal doubts! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: What usually happens when a hospital runs on a strict blame culture?

options.A: Patients experience fewer adverse events during their hospital stay
options.B: Hospital management fixes underlying system problems much faster
options.C: Nurses communicate more openly with physicians about patient care
options.D: Staff hide mistakes and near-misses out of fear of punishment

explanation: When people are terrified of being punished, natural survival instincts kick in and mistakes get swept under the rug.

question: What is the main purpose of a formative evaluation during your nursing training?

options.A: To determine if a nurse is ready to receive a professional license.
options.B: To assign a final grade at the very end of a nursing program.
options.C: To compare a student's score against national averages.
options.D: To provide ongoing feedback and guide student improvement during learning.

explanation: Formative evaluations are like friendly practice checkpoints—they happen along the way to help you catch mistakes and grow before the final exams!

question: What is the giveaway feature of a closed continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) setup?

options.A: Frequent manual disconnection of the drainage bag

options.C: A syringe used every hour to flush out old urine

question: Why shouldn't you squeeze a manual resuscitator bag way too hard during ventilation?

options.A: It causes the oxygen tank to explode
options.B: It instantly damages the heart muscle
options.C: It prevents carbon dioxide from leaving the room
options.D: It can force air into the stomach and cause vomiting

explanation: Squeezing too hard opens up the pathway to the stomach. Filling the stomach with air is a quick ticket to vomiting and aspiration—definitely something we want to avoid!

question: What is the usual daily fat limit for a strict low-fat therapeutic diet?

options.A: Exactly zero grams per day
options.B: Less than 20 grams per day
options.C: Around 70 to 100 grams daily
options.D: Up to 50 percent of total calories

explanation: You got this! A strict low-fat diet keeps fat under 20 grams daily. Eating completely zero fat is almost impossible with natural foods.

question: A patient with a deep, dirty wound hasn't had a tetanus shot in 10 years. The doctor orders a tetanus vaccine AND tetanus immune globulin. Why give the immune globulin?

options.A: To stimulate the patient's innate physical barriers in the skin and mucous membranes

options.C: To provide immediate, short-term protection against toxins while the vaccine takes effect
options.D: To permanently replace the patient's bone marrow cells with donor tissue

explanation: The immune globulin gives instant borrowed antibodies to fight fast-acting toxins right now, while waiting for the actual vaccine to stimulate the patient's own body to make long-term defense.

question: How is low-level radioactive waste managed right after it is generated?

options.A: Mixed right inside the ordinary household rubbish bags
options.B: Stored in shielded containers until its radioactivity naturally fades
options.C: Flushed down the sluice room toilet with running water
options.D: Burned openly in the hospital yard to save space

explanation: Radioactivity gets weaker over time on its own. Storing the waste in special shielded containers lets it cool down to safe levels before disposal.

question: What is a major sign that a patient is struggling to breathe during an emergency check?

options.A: A calm, relaxed face
options.B: Warm, dry skin with pink nail beds
options.C: A steady pulse of 72 beats per minute
options.D: Working hard to breathe and low oxygen saturation

explanation: You nailed it! When a patient is visibly struggling for breath and their oxygen levels drop, it's a clear warning sign that their breathing needs urgent help.

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's medication list before starting them on calcium supplements?

options.A: Calcium completely neutralizes the effects of all known blood pressure medications.
options.B: Calcium interferes with the liver enzymes that process daily vitamins.
options.C: Calcium increases the rate at which the kidneys excrete water-soluble drugs.
options.D: Calcium can bind to certain antibiotics in the gut and stop them from working.

explanation: Spot on! Calcium binds with certain drugs (like tetracyclines) in the stomach, forming a combo your body can't absorb. Always check for drug interactions!

question: Which type of sensory receptors inside the ear pick up sound and movement?

options.A: Chemoreceptors
options.B: Photoreceptors
options.C: Thermoreceptors
options.D: Mechanoreceptors

explanation: Think 'mechanical'! Mechanoreceptors respond to physical forces like sound waves and fluid movement in the ear.

question: In healthcare, what does EHR 'interoperability' mean?

options.A: Patients can print their own paper charts at home using a printer
options.B: All nurses in a hospital use the exact same brand of computer mouse
options.C: Hospital beds automatically update patient weight into the database
options.D: Different health information systems can exchange data accurately

explanation: You got it! Interoperability just means different computer systems can talk to each other and share info smoothly.

question: How do cancer cells frequently manipulate apoptosis to survive and multiply?

options.A: They trigger excessive external death receptor signals
options.B: They replace damaged mitochondria with healthy ones
options.C: They mutate regulatory genes to evade programmed cell death
options.D: They speed up the intrinsic pathway to destroy healthy tissue

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier faced by patients needing rehabilitation?

options.A: Physical barriers like stairs and narrow doors
options.B: Negative cultural beliefs and social stigma
options.C: Excessive availability of trained therapists in rural areas
options.D: High financial costs for care and equipment

question: A ward normally discharges 5 patients a morning, but today 12 left at once because a visiting consultant cleared them all. What kind of variation is this?

options.A: Common cause variation
options.B: Random statistical noise
options.C: Normal baseline fluctuation
options.D: Special cause variation

question: Which group forms the backbone of direct healthcare delivery in Nigerian primary clinics?

options.A: International policy makers
options.B: Hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses and midwives
options.D: Pharmaceutical manufacturers

question: Why is family caregiver education such a vital part of home health nursing?

options.A: Caregivers are legally required to pass nursing board examinations
options.B: Caregivers handle daily care routines during the many hours professionals are absent
options.C: Physicians require family members to sign off on all medical orders
options.D: Education allows family members to replace paid aides entirely

explanation: Because healthcare staff are only present briefly, family caregivers must be taught how to manage routines safely when alone. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)

question: A nursing lecturer uses a physical heart model to explain blood flow to students with different learning styles. Which group benefits most from handling and examining this model directly?

options.A: Auditory learners
options.B: Kinesthetic learners
options.C: Visual learners
options.D: Reading learners

explanation: Kinesthetic learners learn best by touching, moving, and interacting physically with materials and models during a demonstration. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h2)

question: Which activity is an effective way to reach a large group of people during a community mental health campaign?

options.A: Market square talks and radio awareness programs
options.B: Locking patients inside a quiet room
options.C: Destroying traditional medicine books
options.D: Waiting quietly at the clinic for someone to walk in

explanation: Reaching out through public spaces and mass media ensures that mental health messages reach everyday community members where they gather. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the main reason for doing a community diagnosis?

options.A: To increase hospital admission rates across the state
options.B: To understand root causes of health issues and plan interventions
options.C: To replace individual clinical nursing practice completely
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor environmental sanitation

explanation: Exactly! Just like checking a patient's vitals before giving medicine, a community diagnosis helps you find the root problem so you can plan the right solution.

question: When healthcare workers rely on 'tradition,' what is their main mindset?

options.A: Only randomized controlled trials can guide nursing care
options.B: We do it this way because we have always done it this way
options.C: Personal gut feelings are more reliable than textbooks
options.D: Every patient requires a completely unique laboratory workup

explanation: Tradition leans heavily on past habits and routines rather than checking if newer, better methods are available.

question: When handling an emergency family planning complication, what extra communication duty does the nurse have?

options.A: Instructing the client to keep all information a secret
options.B: Posting the client's medical details on social media for donations
options.C: Calling or notifying the receiving facility in advance
options.D: Waiting for three days before writing the referral note

explanation: For urgent cases, advance communication ensures the receiving team prepares emergency equipment and bed space before arrival. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: What does de-identifying a dataset involve?

options.A: Deleting all outliers and missing values from the study
options.B: Removing direct identifiers like patient names and hospital numbers
options.C: Publishing raw patient records in public journals
options.D: Converting all numerical data into categorical scales

explanation: De-identification protects patient privacy by stripping away personal details and replacing them with anonymous tracking numbers. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why do nurses need to know about parasitic ova?

options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure of infected patients
options.C: To synthesize new anti-parasitic medications in the lab
options.D: To help confirm parasite infections through lab results

explanation: Recognizing ova helps you read lab reports and understand how these little bugs cause trouble in patients. Great job!

question: What is the primary goal of community mobilisation?

options.A: Enforcing strict national health laws in rural villages
options.B: Replacing traditional healers with modern medical doctors
options.C: Collecting financial taxes for local health clinics
options.D: Empowering community members to solve local problems together

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on bringing people together so they can take charge of their own health issues and find local solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h1)

question: Who holds overall administrative and clinical responsibility for running a hospital ward?

options.A: The senior ward orderly
options.B: The Chief Medical Director
options.C: The hospital head pharmacist
options.D: The Ward Manager or Nursing Officer in Charge

explanation: The Ward Manager handles staff scheduling, clinical standards, and general administrative duties on the unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: What happens if hazardous waste accidentally gets thrown into the same bin as ordinary office paper?

options.B: The total volume of waste instantly decreases by half

question: What is the biggest reason why survivors of violence often find it hard to speak up right away?

options.A: Forgetfulness
options.B: Strict hospital policies
options.C: Lack of symptoms

question: Why is obtaining informed consent mandatory before conducting any clinical examination or procedure?

question: Before giving an antibiotic, a nurse scans the patient's wristband and the drug barcode with a handheld scanner. What is this safety step called?

question: Why does your nose feel so stuffy and congested when you catch a cold?

question: What is a common headache when buying advanced medical machines in developing economies?

question: How is a nursing diagnosis different from a medical diagnosis?

question: What is the biggest myth driving the medicalisation of FGM?

question: A nurse manager wants a new pressure sore prevention check to stick. What is the most effective strategy?

question: What is a major plus for local farmers when they use short food supply chains?

question: Long ago, during the demonological era, what did people generally believe caused mental illness?

question: Why must community health nurses work closely with WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) teams in an IDP camp?

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to open a patient's electronic health record?

question: What usually happens when a clinic doesn't have enough staff according to PHC standards?

options.A: Increased funding from international donor organizations

options.D: Staff burnout and reduced quality of care for patients

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

question: How can a growing economy help reduce the 'brain drain' of health professionals leaving Nigeria?

question: Why is maintaining proper staff-to-child ratios important for quality assurance?

question: Why do patients with severe metabolic acidosis often end up with high blood potassium?

question: When a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grows, what does it usually mean for the government?

question: Why is a literature review considered weak if it only lists article summaries one by one?

question: Which factor represents part of the physical school health environment?

question: Where would you mostly find a clinical dietitian working?

question: What is 'click fatigue' in the context of electronic health records?

question: What is the main public health goal when treating an infected person who is carrying a pathogen?

question: A patient is having a severe panic attack, breathing fast, and crying out in fear. What is your best first nursing action?

question: How does a rigid professional hierarchy negatively impact patient safety?
